chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Maryam al-Ansari, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام:
Concerning two men who together cut off the hand of a man.

He عليه السلام said: “If he wishes to cut off both of their hands, he must pay to them the compensation for one hand, and they divide it between themselves, then he may cut off both of them. And if he wishes, he may take from them the compensation for his hand. Then if he cuts off the hand of one of them, the one whose hand was not cut off must pay to the one whose hand was cut off one quarter of the compensation.”

key_terms.دِيَةَ يَدٍ: the blood-compensation due for one hand
key_terms.دِيَةَ يَدِهِ: the compensation for his own hand
key_terms.رُبُعَ الدِّيَةِ: one quarter of the full compensation
key_terms.قَطْعِ يَدِ رَجُلٍ: the severing of a man's hand

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when two men jointly cut off one man’s hand in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about two assailants who jointly sever the hand of one victim. It explains the victim’s options between qisas and monetary compensation, and clarifies how liability is adjusted if retaliation is carried out against only one of the two offenders.
